description: Regression pins for the HAVING-past-paging defect family: found 2026-08-10, FIND symbols + HAVING + ORDER BY name silently dropped qualifying rows (ASC returned 3 of 7, DESC 1 of 7 on forgeql-pub.frozen, at limits both above and below the top-K threshold) while path/lines orderings answered correctly. Fixed in 0.159.0 (2026-08-11): the name streams, the running top-K trim, the segment fetch cap and the in-memory backend early exit are all gated on HAVING being absent through one shared predicate. Nothing pinned the fix from the query side until these cases, and they reach only the columnar route — all three golden corpora carry a .forgeql.yaml, so the in-memory backend's own early exit stays unpinned here — narrow and broad, both directions, on all three golden corpora. If one of these goes red, a paging stage has started shedding rows a later HAVING still needed.

cases.name: having_with_name_asc_returns_every_survivor
cases.description: The original repro, broad: 7 functions have lines > 150 on this corpus; ORDER BY name ASC used to return 3. LIMIT 1001 is above TOPK_THRESHOLD, so the running trim is not armed — the loss was in the name-ordered path itself.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE fql_kind = 'function' HAVING lines > 150 ORDER BY name ASC LIMIT 1001

cases.name: having_with_name_desc_returns_every_survivor
cases.description: The worse direction: DESC used to return 1 of 7. The first row pins that the ordering is really descending, not just complete.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE fql_kind = 'function' HAVING lines > 150 ORDER BY name DESC LIMIT 1001

cases.name: having_with_name_asc_keeps_an_honest_total_on_a_narrow_page
cases.description: Narrow: a page smaller than the answer still reports the whole answer in total. The live-repo shape of the same defect returned 0 rows at small limits.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE fql_kind = 'function' HAVING lines > 150 ORDER BY name ASC LIMIT 3

cases.name: control_the_corpus_holds_seven_having_survivors
cases.description: Anchors the three cases above through an ordering that never dropped rows: if this control moves, the corpus drifted, not the fix.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE fql_kind = 'function' HAVING lines > 150 ORDER BY path ASC LIMIT 1001

cases.name: having_with_name_asc_is_complete_on_a_c_corpus
cases.description: Same shape at 3.06M rows: two functions exceed 900 lines on zephyr-andre.frozen.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE fql_kind = 'function' HAVING lines > 900 ORDER BY name ASC LIMIT 1001

cases.name: having_with_name_desc_is_complete_on_a_c_corpus
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE fql_kind = 'function' HAVING lines > 900 ORDER BY name DESC LIMIT 1001

cases.name: having_with_name_asc_narrow_page_keeps_the_total_on_a_c_corpus
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE fql_kind = 'function' HAVING lines > 900 ORDER BY name ASC LIMIT 1

cases.name: having_with_name_asc_is_complete_on_a_python_corpus
cases.description: The threshold was 14000 and the two survivors were CommonTemplate and TestExport — decorated CLASSES that answered as functions because the wrapper node was mapped to `function`. With that row gone no function is anywhere near 14000, so the case would have pinned an empty answer, which cannot fail for the reason it exists. Re-aimed at a threshold that keeps a closed survivor set.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE fql_kind = 'function' HAVING lines > 1500 ORDER BY name ASC LIMIT 1001

cases.name: having_with_name_desc_narrow_page_keeps_the_total_on_a_python_corpus
cases.description: Re-aimed with the case above, and for the same reason.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE fql_kind = 'function' HAVING lines > 1500 ORDER BY name DESC LIMIT 1
